summary: Ann Appleby Hazlewood specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a Master of Arts at the Australian National University, supervised by Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus (attested 1983).
Ann Gleig works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal.

Ann Grodzins Gold is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Chicago (~1978–1984). She held posts at Cornell University (~1987–1993) and Syracuse University, where she became Professor of Religion and Anthropology around 1993.

Ann Heirman is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She worked at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and Ghent University (2003–2012), where she became professor of Chinese language and culture and head of Buddhist studies around 2000.
Ann Laura Stoler is a historian who studied at Columbia University (~1974–1982). She held posts at the University of Michigan (1989–2003) and The New School (2004).

Anna Aurelia Esposito specializes in Indology. She studied at Heidelberg University and completed an MA at the University of Tübingen (ending 1998), later serving as Assistant Professor of Indology at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015).

Anna Balikci Denjongpa works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London under Lionel Caplan, also studying under traditional teachers Lopen Dugyal and Gorlok Tulku, and became Research Coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (2002).

Anna Filigenzi works in archaeology, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She was a member of IsMEO (1984), directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003), and held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2002) and Federico II (attested 2021).
Anna M. Shields is a Sinologist who held posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and Princeton University (~2015).
Anna Madelyn Hennessey works in religious studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara, under the supervision of William F. Powell (attested 2011).

Anna Sawerthal is a scholar of Tibetology. She earned an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Johanna Buß, and a PhD at Heidelberg University supervised by Birgit Kellner and Roland Wenzlhuemer, also learning from Dawa Tsering and Norbu Tashi.
Anna Seidel was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Between ~1963 and 1968, she studied under Maxime Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein.

Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1972–1976). She held academic appointments at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1990–1998) and New York University (~1998).

Anna-Pya Sjödin works in Indology and philosophy. She completed a PhD at Uppsala University by 2007, supervised by Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, and was taught by Klas Hagren and Barbro Eriksson.

Anne Carolyn Klein specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, educated at Binghamton, Wisconsin-Madison, and Virginia. She held posts at Harvard (~1987–1989), Rice University (~1989), and founded the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism (~1996).

Anne Casile works in Indology and archaeology. She was an AHRC research assistant at the British Museum (~2008–2010) and held a post at the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development (~2011).

Anne E. Monius was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Harvard (~1989–1997) under Diana L. Eck and Kausalya Hart. She taught at the University of Virginia (~1997–2002) before becoming professor of South Asian religions at Harvard (2002).

Anne Feldhaus is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Manhattanville University (~1967–1971) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976), and held a post at Arizona State University (~1981).

Anne Hardgrove is a historian and Indologist who studied at Carleton College (~1987–1991) and the University of Michigan (~1992–1999). She held a post at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.

Anne M. Blackburn works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. She completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago (~1989–1996) and was appointed Assistant Professor of Religion at Cornell University (~2001).
